title.narrative: Bright Future in Agriculture - South (BFA - South): Enhancing employability and food security in Ethiopia through quality ATVETs in horticulture

description.narrative:
The proposed project must contribute to the following objective:
Contribute to End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture (SDG 2) and ensuring availability and sustainable management of waler for Clll (SDG 6).
The proposed project must contribute to the following long-term impact:
Promole agricultural growth: Creole ecologically sustainable food systems; Water efficiency in agriculture increased.
Medium-term impact that will contribute to this:
(l) Education system (TVET/HE) is of good quality, relevant and accessible (SDG 4): (Il) Partnerships between persons and organisations are inclusive and sustainable (SDG17): (Ill) Organisations key to (sectoral) inclusive development of partner countries are strengthened by inflow of enhanced workíorce.
Outcomes:
TVET/HE organisations (in the selected partner countries and in NL) perform better their core tasks, firmly embedded in their environment (in line with country / regional specific labour market needs & aiming at inclusiveness) .
To that end, the following output(s) must be achieved by the end of the project:
1 . Strengthening the capabilities of ATVET/Polytechnic teachers to ímplement gender transformative Occupational Standards for (organic) horticultural programmes with an emphasis on practical approaches and teaching methodologies, waler management, technologíes to increase productivity in an eco-friendly manner, inclusive value chain innovations (marketing, value addition, safety standards) nutrition and hands-on capacity;
1. The regional Agricultural bureau SNNPR as a regulatory body is strengthened and ATVETS/Polytechnics in the axis Addis - Hawassa - Arba Minch are better capacitated to perform market oriented, inclusive and eco-friendly horticulture-, and irrigation training programmes in collaboration with the industry, with adequate practical facilities and increased efficiency of leadership, being positioned to act as models for other ATVETs in the Country; 2. Improving federal level policy / stakeholder cooperation and experience sharing through strengthened linkages of ATVETs/Polytechnics along the axis Addis - Hawassa - Arba Minch corridor with relevant federal agencies, State Minister for TVET, MoA , FTA, FTI all key partners of Bright Future Agriculture (BFA) consortium, the BFA project itself and its triple helix platforms, relevant ceriler of excellences in water and horticulture, private sector (incl. industrial parks), FTCs and other horticulture/irrigation organizations, resulting in a regional triple helix platform that will focus on (organic) horticulture in combination with irrigation, to support collaborative reseorcm, outreach and training to come to future proof nutrition sensitive and eco-friendly horticulture growth and export along this corridor.

comment.narrative: 01-03-2022: The number is increased as the teaching material developed is used across all BFA and BFA-South beneficiary colleges. This is because the horticulture skill sheets developed by the sister BFA project and the BFA-South project are used in common by all the beneficiary colleges in both projects.

12-04-2022: The achievement in year one was already beyond the target set for this indicator as the teacher training and learning materials (TTLM) developed are used across all BFA and BFA-South beneficiary colleges.

title.narrative: A.E.3. Number of staff that have gained qualitative and relevant knowledge and skills to develop and offer the revised/developed study programmes

comment.narrative: 01-03-2022: 25 staff (4% female) have gained relevant knowledge and skills in gender awareness and mainstreaming, teaching material development, labor market needs assessment, internship and apprenticeship. The reason for the deviation is that the trainings were suspended because of the COVID-19 pandemic at least by six months. Some of the training were adapted to an online platform and delivered in October and not included in this report. The low rate of female participation will persist for the foreseeable future because female faculty members are few in the teaching pool. For example out of a total of 280 teachers in the three beneficiary colleges there are only 24 female teachers which is 8.5%.

12-04-2022: The reason is basically due to the Pandemic and they are three folds: 1. All practical Trainings that required physical presence of international experts have to be postponed altogether. 2. Even those training offered by Ethiopian experts were offered late in the reporting period and it was not able to do a second round training 3. Even the number of participants in the offered training have to be cut by half to meet the protocol of the pandemic 4. At times the few teachers in each college have to prepare a number of skill sheets. Thus, if there had been opportunity to distribute the preparation for other teachers, the number of teachers who took part in skill sheet preparation would have been more than that stated here.

title.narrative: A.S.1. Number of beneficiaries in the society reached with knowledge, skills and techniques

comment.narrative: 12-04-2022: In Arba Minch triple Helix, we work with 26 platforms members coming from public institutions, academia, and the private sector. At this moment, the workshops organized by the platform create the opportunity of sharing knowledge among the participants that could improve the services each actor play to solve different problems in the fruit value chain. The platform will reach more beneficiaries when it starts dissemination of the technology being developed.

title.narrative: A.R.3. Number of relevant innovations

comment.narrative: 12-04-2022: The Arba Minch triple helix platform envisions to introduce 3 postharvest technologies namely harvesting, collapsible plastic crate and ripening technology. The platform with Wolyata Rural Technology Research Centre has produced a prototype of a wooden crate and harvesting technology. A harvesting technology is developed, the product is tasted on the market and now the product is being improved based on the feedback from farmers. The ripening technology was intended to be used by framers to properly ripen their fruits before they sell to the customers. However, we found out that ripening technology is not appropriate as most commercial farmers sell unripen fruits. Selling ripen fruits increases fruit losses as the fruits are transported long distance to reach to final consumers.

title.narrative: A.O.11. Number of organisations with policies and procedures to ensure an environment which is gender sensitive

comment.narrative: 12-04-2022: The full impact of the training to put in place a gender sensitive environment meant to happen in conjunction with the full ownership of the Roadmap and the policy shifts that are outlined in the policy brief. The validation of the Roadmap has happened shortly after the end of this reporting period.

title.narrative: A.S.3. Number of students performing an internship or practical work

comment.narrative: 40% female

12-04-2022: The number of students/internship is reduced for several reasons: there were shortage of hosting companies that are able to fulfil the skill training required from the interns and have a full-fledged company structure to let the interns experience the world of work environment; the costs involved for 1 internship were considerably higher than originally budgeted; the work needed to manage 1 internship successfully has been enormous, which forced to lower the numbers to keep it manageable. If budget allows, a second round of internships will be organized in 2022. In addition, originally not planned in the project, was the teachers’ internship. This was put in place partly for the teachers themselves to have the internship experience so that they would appreciate it for its sustainability.
40% female

title.narrative: A.O.6. Number of facilities established/strengthened

comment.narrative: 12-04-2022: There is a delay in the utilization of the investment budget of which Euro 123, 000 has been utilized out of the investment budget outlay of EUR 275,000. The reason for the delay in the utilization of the investment budget is the much government bureaucratic hurdle one faces in undertaking domestic purchase. However, there are a number of purchases that are in the pipeline or recently completed as this report is being made (such as lab equipment, drip irrigation facilities and other farm equipment)
